Writing a sheet

A sheet is a list of statements: given values, equations, and lines such as check and table. Dome solves the equations together, so their order does not matter. Each section below starts from a sheet you can copy into Dome, shows what Dome gives, and then lists the rules.

Equations and units

A gas expands at constant pressure while it does 6 kJ of work on a piston. This sheet finds its final volume and temperature.

p   = 2 [bar]
V_1 = 40 [L]
T_1 = 27 [C]
W   = 6 [kJ]
W = p * (V_2 - V_1)
T_2 / T_1 = V_2 / V_1

Dome gives V_2 = 0.07 m³ and T_2 = 525.26 K, each at the right of the line that finds it. While Auto-solve is checked in the header, Dome solves the sheet after each edit.

  1. Write one statement on each line, or separate statements with semicolons: x = 3; y = 4.
  2. Write an equation as a = b, arranged in any way. An unknown may be on either side, as V_2 is above, and the lines may come in any order.
  3. Write a unit in square brackets after each number: 40 [L]. Dome converts every value to SI as it reads it, so bar, L and kJ can be mixed in one equation.
  4. In a unit, everything after a slash is in the denominator: [kJ/kg·K] is kJ/(kg·K). Units also combine with *, ^ and parentheses, as in [m^3/kg].
  5. A 0 needs no unit. In 0 = Q - W + mdot*(h_1 - h_2), the 0 takes the unit of the other terms. A 0 given for a temperature needs one, since 0 °C and 0 K differ.
  6. To show a value in another unit, divide it by that unit: p_kPa = p / (1 [kPa]) gives 200.
  7. The SI and English buttons in the header set the units Dome shows. With English, the sheet above gives V_2 = 2.472 ft³ and T_2 = 945.47 °R.

Help › Examples › First sheet: equations and units opens this sheet with comments, a temperature change, two unit conversions and a check line.

Temperatures and temperature changes

T_1 = 27 [C]
T_2 = 80 [C]
dT  = T_2 - T_1
T_a = T_1 + 20 [K]
T_m = (T_1 + T_2)/2
r   = T_2 / T_1

Dome gives dT = 53 K, T_a = 47 °C, T_m = 53.5 °C and r = 1.1766.

  1. A number in [C] or [F] is a temperature. A number in [K] or [R] is a temperature or a change, as the equations use it.
  2. Write a change in temperature in [K] or [R]: T_1 + 20 [K] is 20 K above T_1.
  3. Dome holds every temperature in kelvin, so T_2 / T_1 is a ratio of absolute temperatures. Use T_1 itself in every equation, never T_1 + 273.15 [K].
  4. A difference of two temperatures is a change, shown in K. An average, such as (T_1 + T_2)/2, is a temperature. Dome refuses a plain sum, T_1 + T_2.
  5. In a sum or difference, write a [C] or [F] number in parentheses: (25 [C]) + dT. Without them, Dome cannot tell a temperature from a change.
  6. A name makes no difference: dT = 10 [C] is the temperature 10 °C. A change of 10 K is dT = 10 [K].
  7. Dome shows a value in °C only where it is certainly a temperature, such as the T of a state. Other values are shown in K, as T_2 is in the first sheet.
  8. On an English sheet, °F and °R take the places of °C and K.

Comments and sections

%% Boundary work at constant pressure
% Given values
p   = 2 [bar]
V_1 = 40 [L]
W   = 6 [kJ]

%% Final volume
W = p * (V_2 - V_1)    % work done by the gas

Dome gives V_2 = 0.07 m³. Comments and blank lines change nothing in the solve.

  1. Text after % is a comment, on a line of its own or after a statement.
  2. A line that starts with %% begins a section of a published report.
  3. The first section's text is the report's default title, here "Boundary work at constant pressure".

Problems and fixes

This is the first sheet with one more line. Nothing else in the sheet determines dU, so Dome cannot use the last line.

p   = 2 [bar]
V_1 = 40 [L]
T_1 = 27 [C]
W   = 6 [kJ]
W = p * (V_2 - V_1)
T_2 / T_1 = V_2 / V_1
Q = W + dU

nothing determines dU: there are fewer equations than unknowns

The shot shows the same line added to the first example.

  1. A line Dome cannot use is underlined in the sheet. The pointer over the underline shows the message.
  2. The Problems tab lists each error and warning with its line number and message. A click on one moves the cursor to its line.
  3. Each message has an Explain button, which opens the section of this manual that gives its rule.
  4. A message that names an exact rewrite has a button for it, under the message in the sheet and in the Problems tab. The button makes the rewrite as one edit, which ⌘Z undoes.
  5. A message with two rewrites, one for each reading of the line, offers both and makes neither. Press ⌘. to make the rewrite at the cursor, or to open the choice when there are two.

When Dome refuses, below, gives the messages a new sheet meets most often. The Reference page lists every rewrite.

Checks and starting values

Checking a result

p   = 2 [bar]
V_1 = 40 [L]
W   = 6 [kJ]
W = p * (V_2 - V_1)
check V_2 > V_1

Dome gives V_2 = 0.07 m³ and shows "passed" at the right of the check line. With check V_2 < V_1, the line shows "failed".

  1. A check line compares two expressions after the sheet is solved. The comparisons are ==, <=, >=, < and >.
  2. The result appears at the right of the line and under the Checks tab.
  3. The two sides need units that match, as in an equation: check T_1 > 300 needs a unit after the 300.
  4. Dome does not evaluate a check line that has an error on it.

Choosing between two answers

x^2 - 5*x + 6 = 0

Dome gives x = 2 and this warning:

two values of x satisfy this equation, 2 and 3; Dome used 2. A check line such as "check x > 2.5" chooses between them.

With the line check x > 2.5 added, Dome gives x = 3 and no warning.

  1. A check line on the variable chooses between two answers. The warning's button, Add the line "check x > 2.5", writes it below the equation.
  2. Equations solved together are searched too. For x + y = 5 with x*y = 6, both lines name the two solutions, and a check line on x or y chooses.
  3. A value of the other sign is not counted: V_2^2 = 100 [m^2/s^2] gives V_2 = 10 m/s and no warning.
  4. The search can miss a second answer, so a line with no warning may still have one.

Starting values

x^2 - 5*x + 6 = 0
guess x = 2.6

Dome starts x at 2.6 and gives x = 3, with this warning:

two values of x satisfy this equation, 2 and 3; Dome used 3. A check line such as "check x < 2.5" chooses between them.

  1. An unknown alone on one side of its equation, as q in q = h_2 - h_1, is computed at once. For any other unknown, Dome tries a value, sees how far the equation is from holding, and corrects the value until it holds. A guess line sets the first value tried.
  2. Write a guess line only when Dome reports that a solve could not start, or found no solution from its starting values.
  3. A guess line sets only the start. To choose between two answers, write a check line.
  4. Without a guess line, an unknown starts from a value set by its units, never by its name. The Reference page gives the rule.

Functions

A function is a formula written once and used in several places. This one gives a specific heat that rises with temperature.

function cp_air(T) = 1.0 [kJ/kg/K] + 1e-4 [kJ/kg/K^2]*(T - 300 [K])
T_1 = 300 [K]
T_2 = 400 [K]
q = cp_air(T_2)*(T_2 - T_1)

Dome gives q = 101 kJ/kg.

  1. Write a function on one line: the word function, a name, the parameters in parentheses, =, and one expression.
  2. A call gives one argument for each parameter, in order. A call may appear in any equation, state line or check, and an unknown may appear inside it.
  3. The body may use the parameters, numbers with units, math and property functions, other functions of the sheet, and the sheet's variables.
  4. A function cannot call itself, directly or through another function. Its name cannot be a built-in function such as h or ln, a keyword such as state, or a variable of the sheet.
  5. An error inside the body is reported on the line of the call, and the message names the function.

Tables

A table holds rows of numbers, such as rows typed from a property table. Two rows of saturated R-134a give the temperature at which saturated vapor has v = 0.0430 m³/kg, and u there.

table sat : T [C], v_g [m^3/kg], u_g [kJ/kg]
  12, 0.0460, 233.63
  16, 0.0405, 235.78
v_1 = 0.0430 [m^3/kg]
interp(sat, v_g, T = T_2) = v_1
u_2 = interp(sat, u_g, T = T_2)

Dome gives T_2 = 14.182 °C and u_2 = 234.8 kJ/kg.

  1. The header line names the table and each column with its unit.
  2. The rows follow on indented lines, with numbers separated by commas. A blank or unindented line ends the table. A % comment may follow a row.
  3. interp(sat, u_g, T = T_2) is the value of column u_g at T = T_2, by linear interpolation between the two rows around it.
  4. The key column, here T, must increase or decrease throughout. A key outside the table is an error that gives the table's range.
  5. An unknown may be the key, so a table reads in either direction. The first interp line above finds T_2 from v_1.
  6. A column in [C] or [F] holds temperatures. Dome refuses a key for it that is a change in temperature, such as T_b - T_a.
  7. A column in [K] or [R] is read at the key's value in that unit, whether the key is a temperature or a change. With T_1 = 27 [C], the key T = T_1 reads it at 300.15 K. With T_a = 20 °C and T_b = 50 °C, the key dT = T_b - T_a reads it at 30 K.

Integrals and derivatives

An integral or a derivative gives what a sheet has no closed form for. This sheet finds the work of a compression with p V^1.3 constant, and c_p of liquid water at 50 °C as the slope of h.

p_1 = 100 [kPa]; V_1 = 0.1 [m^3]; V_2 = 0.04 [m^3]
C = p_1*V_1^1.3
W = integral(C/V^1.3, V, V_1, V_2)
c_p = der(h(water, p = 1 [bar], T = T), T, 50 [C])

Dome gives W = -10.546 kJ and c_p = 4.1813 kJ/(kg·K).

  1. integral(e, x, a, b) is the integral of the expression e over x from a to b.
  2. der(e, x, c) is the derivative of e with respect to x at x = c.
  3. The variable x belongs to the call. Inside e, its name means the call's variable, and a sheet variable with the same name keeps its value. In the limits, the name means the sheet's variable.
  4. x takes the units of its limits, which must match. An integral is in the units of e times those of x, and a derivative in the units of e over those of x.
  5. e may use the sheet's other variables, functions of the sheet, interp() with x as the key, and property functions with x as an input.
  6. A limit, the point or a variable in e may be an unknown. With W = -15 [kJ] given in place of V_2, the integral line finds V_2 = 0.028981 m³.

When Dome refuses

Each entry gives a sheet, the message Dome shows for it, and what to change. The messages a new sheet meets most often come first.

A number without a unit

T_H = 500 [C]
T_L = 25
eta = 1 - T_L/T_H

this number needs a unit: by the equation on line 3, T_L is a temperature, so write e.g. 25 [C] or 25 [K]

Write the unit you meant. The buttons Write 25 [C] and Write 25 [K] write either one; the two give different values of eta.

Units that do not match

mdot = 2 [kg/s]
h_1 = 300 [kJ/kg]; h_2 = 250 [kJ/kg]
Q = 20 [kW]
W = Q + h_1 - h_2

units do not match: kW + kJ/kg

Every term of a sum or difference needs the same units. Here the enthalpy change needs its mass flow rate: W = Q + mdot*(h_1 - h_2) gives W = 120 kW.

An equation that contradicts the others

p   = 2 [bar]
V_1 = 40 [L]
W   = 6 [kJ]
W = p * (V_2 - V_1)
V_2 = 0.08 [m^3]

this equation contradicts the others (its two sides differ by 13.3 %)

The sheet gives V_2 twice: the work gives 0.07 m³, and the last line 0.08 m³. Remove one of them. An equation that gives nothing new, such as V_2 = V_1 + W/p in place of the last line, gets a warning instead. Its buttons remove a line or make it a check line.

A [C] number in a sum or difference

T_1 = 27 [C]
T_a = T_1 + 20 [C]

a [C] number in a sum or difference could be a temperature or a change in temperature: write a change as 20 [K], or the temperature in parentheses, (20 [C])

For 20 K above T_1, write 20 [K]; the button Write a change as 20 [K] does it. Where both readings fit, as in 25 [C] + dT, the message has a button for each. Choose the one the sheet means.

A temperature converted to kelvin by hand

T_1 = 27 [C]
T_K = T_1 + 273.15 [K]

T_1 is already an absolute temperature: Dome holds every temperature in kelvin and converts [C] and [F] as it reads them, so adding 273.15 [K] counts the offset twice; use T_1 itself

Use T_1 wherever the sheet uses T_K. The button Remove + 273.15 [K] leaves T_K = T_1.

A temperature where a change belongs, or the reverse

T_1 = 27 [C]
T_2 = 80 [C]
T_s = T_1 + T_2

T_2 is a temperature, and this adds it to another temperature; write a change in [K]

For the mean temperature, write (T_1 + T_2)/2; for the change, T_2 - T_1. The reverse slip is a [C] number given for a change: Dome refuses T_2 - T_1 = 30 [C], and its button writes 30 [K].

A result in a unit no quantity has

W_net = 100
h_1 = 300 [kJ/kg]; h_2 = 250 [kJ/kg]
W_net = mdot*(h_1 - h_2)

mdot is in s^2/m^2, a unit no usual quantity has; it depends on W_net, which is given without a unit, so check whether W_net needs one

A number without a unit where no equation requires one is a plain number, so mdot came out in s²/m². Write the unit: with W_net = 100 [kW], Dome gives mdot = 2 kg/s.

A check written with =

x = 3
check x = 3

a check compares with ==, <=, >=, < or >

Write check x == 3; the button Write == does it. The reverse slip, == in an equation, has a button that writes =.

A key outside a table

table sat : T [C], v_g [m^3/kg], u_g [kJ/kg]
  12, 0.0460, 233.63
  16, 0.0405, 235.78
u_2 = interp(sat, u_g, T = 20 [C])

T = 20 [C] is outside table sat, whose T runs from 12 to 16 [C]

Add rows on both sides of the key, or check the value of the key.

A misspelled keyword

fluid water
stat 1 : p = 1 [bar], x = 1

expected "=" but found "1"

Dome read stat as the name of a variable, so it expected an equation. Correct the spelling to state. The Reference page lists the keywords.

The Math view

The Math view shows the sheet typeset as equations, with the value of each line. The first example's shot above shows it in place of the figure.

  1. The Code and Math buttons in the sheet's header switch the sheet pane between the text and the Math view.
  2. To show the Math view beside the sheet, choose Math in the menu of any other pane.

Keys and completion

Keys are listed as on macOS. On Windows and Linux, Ctrl takes the place of ⌘.

KeysWhat they do
⌘EnterSolve the sheet. In the sweep editor, run the sweep.
⌘.Make the rewrite that the problem at the cursor offers. Where it offers two, open them as a choice: the arrow keys move, Enter makes one and Esc closes the choice.
⌘ZUndo the last edit, a rewrite included.
CtrlSpaceComplete a name, unit or fluid. On macOS, where CtrlSpace often switches the input source, Option` does the same.

The language reference

Help › Reference opens a pane beside the sheet that lists the statements, units, functions and keys. The Reference page of this manual lists the keywords, operators, units, fluids and functions in tables, with the rules in full.
